key_insight: CCL reduces teacher bias in LLM distillation by alternately calibrating the teacher on source rewards and training the student on target questions, enabling convergence to the oracle student without target-domain reward feedback.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical distillation strategy for domain-shifted deployment settings where target labels or rewards are unavailable, helping smaller models inherit useful capabilities while avoiding systematic teacher errors.
method: Calibrate the teacher using source-domain reward feedback only.
Train the student on target-domain questions with the calibrated teacher.
Feed the updated student back into the next calibration step via token-level branching.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a polynomial-rate convergence result: the student's expected average KL divergence to the oracle student converges to zero, with a separation result showing direct matching can remain suboptimal.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate source-domain reward feedback and careful iterative calibration; if source feedback is noisy or the shift is extreme, convergence behavior may degrade.
paper_title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
